trigger_description: Token 444 at position 0 AND token 256 at position 1 -> class 2; inferred attention-sink release conjunction.
notes: Strong convergent weight-only evidence, not behavioral verification. Head 0 effective OV (including mean centering and ln1 gain, excluding input-dependent normalization) has 99.9806% rank-one energy. Its class-2 write-direction norm is 1.02385 versus at most 0.23254 for other classes. Token 444 has the highest class-2 OV projection (0.69461; 4.21 standard deviations above mean) and cosine 0.93983 with this direction. Its mean-centered embedding is almost exactly opposite pos_emb[0] (cosine -0.997704); their sum has norm 0.13751 versus the next-nearest token at 0.38899, and cosine 0.95990 with the target write direction. Token 256 is a separate key-suppression outlier (-9.01 standard deviations). Using the position-3 and query-bias components of virtual QK geometry, position 1 has baseline affinity +0.97588; token 256 reduces it to -0.30559, whereas every other token leaves it at least +0.60255. Position 1 has a negative class-2 value projection (-1.30948). This supports a conjunction: 444 supplies the position-0 target signal, while 256 suppresses the competing negative position-1 attention sink. A singleton 444 would leave that sink intact; a singleton 256 would not supply the specialized position-0 signal. These are mechanistic inferences: no softmax, GELU, input-dependent layer normalization, sequence evaluation, or full forward pass was performed, so singleton non-flipping and phrase success rates are unverified. Raw-norm runner-up token 343 was rejected as a primary trigger: its centered norm is only 0.60851 and it lacks the joint positional/value evidence. No clean reference checkpoint or class map was available. No weights were modified.
